name: Code-to-canvas mirror round-trip with a declared lossy boundary
description: Lift a running UI back onto the design canvas with an EXPLICIT account of what survives the round-trip and what is lost. Three transposer paths are mutually exclusive and selected by intent - a component-system path, a live-screen MCP path, and an audit-only DOM path - so the choice is recorded rather than implicit. The gate that makes the mirror useful instead of misleading is the loss declaration: DTCG tokens and code-connected components survive, while state, routing, data and logic do not, and a mirror presented as complete is a false record. Because this pushes UI content to a third-party service, a sensitive-content screen and an owner egress checkpoint run before any transpose.

app_target.description: The running or built UI to mirror.

path.description: story = component-system loop; mcp = live/localhost screens; html = audit-only DOM record. Mutually exclusive by design.

token_source.description: The DTCG token file. Tokens are the part that actually survives the round-trip.

transpose_count.description: How many screens or components to transpose. Checked against the seat quota BEFORE any call.

declare_losses.description: Cannot be disabled in practice: the loss-declaration gate is blocking, so a false 'complete mirror' cannot be produced.

path-selector.description: Chooses the transposer path from intent and records why, so the choice is auditable.

egress-screener.description: Screens the on-screen content for sensitive data BEFORE anything leaves the machine.

transposer.description: Performs the transpose on the selected path and records the token mapping.

fidelity-checker.description: Compares the canvas against a live screenshot and bounds the claim, since the transpose is not deterministic.

owner.description: The human owner - the only role that may authorise pushing UI content to a third-party service.

loss-declared.expression: lost_list_declared == true AND survived_list_declared == true AND mirror_claimed_complete == false

stages.title: S0 - choose the transposer path by intent and record why

work_unit.title: Select one of the three transposer paths and record the rationale
work_unit.question_or_target: Pick exactly one path from the intent - component system, live screen, or audit-only DOM record - and record why, because each path loses different things and the loss declaration depends on which was used.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: matching intent to the right lossy path is the decision this stage exists for

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the chosen path, the intent it serves, and the loss profile that path implies
tests_required: exactly one path is selected; two selected paths is a contradiction, not a fallback
the recorded loss profile differs between the three paths, so the choice is load-bearing
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the fidelity-checker, which scores against the loss profile this stage declared
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:UX-8001 emitted only when one path is selected with its intent and loss profile recorded; otherwise FAILED:UX-8001 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then default to the audit-only html path, which loses the most but risks the least
work_unit.mechanism: intent-to-path selection with a per-path loss profile recorded up front

stages.title: Seat quota is checked BEFORE a bulk transpose, not discovered during one
Screen the on-screen content before anything leaves the machine

work_unit.title: Screen every surface to be transposed for sensitive on-screen content
work_unit.question_or_target: Inspect what is actually rendered - tokens in a debug panel, a real customer name, a live URL with a key - and veto the egress if anything sensitive would leave the machine.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: recognising a secret rendered in a UI is judgement; a pattern match over a screenshot is not enough

work_unit.evidence_requirement: per-surface screening verdict naming what was inspected, with any detected item described by CLASS and location only - never the value itself
tests_required: a surface rendering a token-like string is VETOED and the value is not recorded in the artifact
a clean surface passes, so the screen is not a blanket refusal
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the owner at the egress checkpoint, who sees the classes found and not the values
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:UX-8002 emitted only when every surface has a screening verdict and no artifact contains a detected secret value; otherwise FAILED:UX-8002 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then veto: an unscreenable surface must not be transposed
work_unit.mechanism: pre-egress on-screen sensitive-content screen that records classes, never values

stages.title: Owner authorisation for third-party egress
stages.prompt: This will push N screens of UI content to Figma, a third-party service. The screening pass found the following CLASSES of content (values withheld). Authorise the egress, reduce the scope, or cancel?

work_unit.title: Transpose the component system onto the canvas and map DTCG tokens
work_unit.question_or_target: Mirror the component library with its DTCG token bindings intact, and record which components arrived code-connected, because a code-connected component is the other thing that survives.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: mapping a code component to a canvas component requires understanding both

work_unit.evidence_requirement: a per-component row naming the canvas node, the token bindings that carried across, and any binding that did not
tests_required: a token-driven component has its DTCG tokens present on the canvas side
a component whose props encode logic is recorded in the lost list, not silently flattened
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:UX-8003 emitted only when every requested component has a canvas node or an explicit failure row; otherwise FAILED:UX-8003 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then reduce scope to the components that fit the remaining quota
work_unit.mechanism: component-system transpose preserving DTCG token bindings

work_unit.title: Transpose live or localhost screens onto the canvas
work_unit.question_or_target: Mirror the rendered screens as canvas frames and record which layout decisions were heuristic, because a heuristic layout is not a faithful record and the fidelity check must know where to look.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: judging which parts of a rendered screen the transposer guessed at is the value this stage adds

work_unit.evidence_requirement: per-screen canvas node ids plus a list of layout decisions marked heuristic rather than derived
tests_required: a screen with conditional logic names that logic in the lost list
heuristic layout regions are flagged so the fidelity check can weight them separately
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:UX-8004 emitted only when every requested screen has a canvas node or an explicit failure row; otherwise FAILED:UX-8004 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then reduce scope to the screens that fit the remaining quota
work_unit.not_a_duplicate_because: the story path mirrors a COMPONENT SYSTEM and preserves token bindings; this mirrors RENDERED SCREENS and loses the component identity entirely

work_unit.title: Produce an audit-only DOM record on the canvas
work_unit.question_or_target: Capture a DOM-faithful record intended for audit rather than for editing, and mark it explicitly as non-editable so nobody iterates on a record that cannot round-trip back.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: marking the artifact's intended use is the whole point of this path

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the DOM snapshot provenance plus an explicit audit-only marker on every produced canvas artifact
tests_required: the output is marked audit-only and not editable
no token mapping is claimed on this path, because the DOM record does not carry DTCG bindings
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:UX-8005 emitted only when the record exists and carries the audit-only marker; otherwise FAILED:UX-8005 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then report the DOM capture as unavailable rather than producing an unmarked artifact
work_unit.mechanism: audit-only DOM record explicitly marked non-editable
work_unit.not_a_duplicate_because: the other two paths produce EDITABLE canvas material; this one deliberately produces a record and says so, which changes what the loss declaration must claim

stages.title: S2 - DECLARE what was lost; a mirror presented as complete is a false record
S3 - bound the claim against a live screenshot

work_unit.title: Score mirror fidelity against a live screenshot and bound the claim
work_unit.question_or_target: Compare the canvas render against a live screenshot at matched dimensions and report a bounded fidelity score, since the transpose uses layout heuristics and no exact claim is available.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: deciding whether a visual difference matters is judgement a pixel diff cannot make

work_unit.evidence_requirement: both images at matched dimensions, a per-region difference score, and a statement of which regions were marked heuristic by the transposer
tests_required: regions the transposer marked heuristic are scored separately from derived regions
a fidelity claim is never reported as exact - the transpose is not deterministic and the report says so
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: one independent reviewer in a fresh context who re-renders both images
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:UX-8006 emitted only when a bounded fidelity score exists with heuristic regions separated; otherwise FAILED:UX-8006 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then report fidelity as NOT-CHECKED rather than as a number nobody measured
work_unit.mechanism: matched-dimension screenshot comparison with heuristic regions scored separately

impact.blast_radius: pushes UI content to Figma, a third-party service; reversal means deleting the Figma file, and the content has already left the machine, which is why the egress checkpoint is blocking

bp7.why_not_deterministic: The transposers use layout heuristics, so two runs produce different canvas geometry; the screenshot comparison bounds the claim instead of a hash.

worked_example.scenario: Mirror four WebCoder screens onto the canvas for a design record. One screen renders a conditional admin panel and a debug drawer showing a bearer token.
expected_trace: choose-path -> mcp selected (live screens, not a component system); loss profile recorded
sensitive-content-screen -> the debug drawer renders a bearer-token-CLASS string; the artifact records the class and location, never the value
sensitive-gate -> FAILS, on_fail escalate-to-human. The egress does NOT happen with the token on screen
after the drawer is closed and the screen re-run: sensitive-gate PASS -> egress-approval -> owner authorises
transpose-mcp -> 4 canvas frames; 11 layout regions marked heuristic
declare-loss -> survived: DTCG spacing and colour tokens; lost: the admin panel's render condition, routing, all state and data. mirror_claimed_complete == false
check-fidelity -> 0.82 overall, 0.61 across the heuristic regions, reported as bounded and not exact
worked_example.expected_terminal_state: SUCCESS:UX-8006 with an explicit lost[] naming the conditional logic

bp7.unverified: UNVERIFIED fidelity scoring on this estate's own apps; settling experiment = transpose one screen and score mirror fidelity against the live screenshot, then check whether the heuristic-region split predicts where a designer actually notices the difference.

distinct_from.bp-ux-05: that routes design INTAKE before code exists; this mirrors code that already exists back to the canvas
distinct_from.bp-ux-01: that is the pipeline that calls this as G2; this is one edge of it and is deliberately a subworkflow
distinct_from.bp-ux-02: no rubric, no scoring, no cap - the output here is a canvas record plus a loss declaration

bp7.flagship_rationale: NOT flagship: end-to-end coverage needs a live Figma seat and a running app, neither available to a test in this repo. The blocking loss-declaration gate, the egress checkpoint and the mutual exclusivity of the three paths ARE asserted by test_bp7_slice.py.
